claims.text: A Pulumi package is the unit of versioning and distribution, and the components inside it inherit the package's version.
Pulumi recommends structuring Git repositories for publishing packages per the strategies in this guide (one package per repository).
Following the recommended repository practices improves the reliability, maintainability, and delivery speed of packages an organization builds and consumes.
Pulumi packages come in two flavors (source-based and executable-based), and each is versioned and released differently.
A source-based plugin package is distributed as source code in a Git repository.
A source-based package's version is the Git tag on its repository.

Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow (apply a semver Git tag, then run pulumi package publish), typically performed by a CI/CD pipeline that runs on tag.
Publishing a source-based package to the Private Registry requires applying a semver Git tag (e.g., v1.2.3) to the repository.
`pulumi package publish` sends the package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.
The publish step often runs automated tests before publishing.
Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Private Registry.
Source-based packages referenced directly from a Pulumi.yaml file can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), regardless of whether it is a valid semantic version.

An executable-based plugin package is distributed as a pre-built plugin binary, typically alongside per-language SDKs published to package feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, the Go module proxy, or private equivalents).
An executable-based package's version is the version embedded in the published binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can additionally publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
Executable-based package releases are produced by a CI/CD pipeline that builds the plugin, generates the SDKs, and pushes everything to the relevant feeds.
In both source-based and executable-based cases, the released artifact is a single, semantically-versioned Pulumi package.
A repository should contain exactly one Pulumi package, regardless of package type; this is Pulumi's recommendation.
A repository containing multiple packages must either release them in lockstep or invent per-package release tooling that conflicts with how Pulumi naturally consumes packages.
Multiple components inside a single Pulumi package are supported and expected, and ship together at the package's version.
The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with supporting components needed to secure and operate it.
One PulumiPlugin.yaml at the repository root defines the package, with components living alongside it.
Using a single monorepo containing one giant package for all of an organization's components is technically possible, but Pulumi does not recommend it.
When unrelated components share a package, every release of the package versions every component the same way regardless of whether each changed, which violates semver.

In a package with two unrelated components, an enhancement to ComponentA yields a v1.1.0 release and a breaking change to ComponentB yields v2.0.0, decoupling version numbers from each component's evolution.
Splitting unrelated components across separate right-sized packages preserves the semver contract.
The Pulumi IDP Private Registry concept page exists at /docs/idp/concepts/private-registry/.
The pulumi package publish CLI reference page exists at /docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_package_publish/.
A Publishing packages guide exists at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/packages/publishing-packages/.
